## Who is the 11x34.5x1a MERV 13 best for?

[MERV 13 filters](https://filterking.com/air-filter/merv-13) are ideal for homes where air quality is a top priority. They're ideal for households
with allergies, asthma, and respiratory issues. Using a MERV 13 filter can also help improve indoor air
quality in households with immunocompromised family members and homes with pets that require extra
protection.


Our MERV 13 filters are suitable for urban homes near traffic and light commercial spaces, such as
offices or medical waiting rooms and even clinics in some instances. Shared living spaces and rental
units may benefit from MERV 13 filters, as the filter is designed to capture even more particles than
alternative ratings.

## How to find your air filter size?

Check the label on your current filter or use a tape measure to get the exact length, width, and
depth before
selecting your size.

![nominal vs actual air filter size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-img-custom-filters-find-size.webp)

### ![Nominal Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-nominal-size.svg)  Nominal size

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x34.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x34.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x34.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x34.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x34.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x34.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x34.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x34.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## How to find your air filter size?

Check the label on your current filter or use a tape measure to get the exact length, width, and
depth before
selecting your size.

![nominal vs actual air filter size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-img-custom-filters-find-size.webp)

### ![Nominal Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-nominal-size.svg)  Nominal size

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x34x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x34x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x34x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x34x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x34x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x34x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x34x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x34x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x34x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x34x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x34x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x34x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x34x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x34x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x34x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x34x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x35.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x35.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x35.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x35.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x35.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x35.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x35.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x35.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## How to find your air filter size?

depth before

### ![Nominal Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-nominal-size.svg)  Nominal size

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x35.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x35.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x35.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x35.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x35.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x35.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x35.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x35.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x35x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x35x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x35x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x35x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x35x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x35x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x35x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x35x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x35x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x35x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x35x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x35x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

### How often should I replace my 11x36.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x36.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x36.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x36.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

Higher-quality 11x36.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x36.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x36.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x36.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x36.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x36.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x36.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x36.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x36.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x36.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x36.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x36.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## How to find your air filter size?

Check the label on your current filter or use a tape measure to get the exact length, width, and
depth before
selecting your size.

![nominal vs actual air filter size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-img-custom-filters-find-size.webp)

### ![Nominal Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-nominal-size.svg)  Nominal size

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x36x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x36x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x36x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x36x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x36x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x36x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x36x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x36x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x37.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x37.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x37.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x37.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x37.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x37.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x37.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x37.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x37.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x37.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x37.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x37.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x37.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x37.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x37.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x37.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## How to find your air filter size?

Check the label on your current filter or use a tape measure to get the exact length, width, and
depth before

![nominal vs actual air filter size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-img-custom-filters-find-size.webp)

### ![Nominal Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-nominal-size.svg)  Nominal size

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x37x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x37x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x37x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x37x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x37x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x37x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x37x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x37x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x38.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x38.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x38.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x38.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x38.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x38.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x38.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x38.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x38.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x38.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x38.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x38.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x38.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x38.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x38.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x38.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## How to find your air filter size?

Check the label on your current filter or use a tape measure to get the exact length, width, and
depth before
selecting your size.

![nominal vs actual air filter size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-img-custom-filters-find-size.webp)

### ![Nominal Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-nominal-size.svg)  Nominal size

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x38x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x38x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x38x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x38x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x38x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x38x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x38x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x38x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x38x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x38x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x38x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x38x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x38x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x38x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x38x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x38x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x39.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x39.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x39.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x39.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x39.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x39.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x39.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x39.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x39.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x39.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x39.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x39.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x39.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x39.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x39.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x39.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x39.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x39.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x39.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x39.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x39.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x39.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x39.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x39.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## How to find your air filter size?

Check the label on your current filter or use a tape measure to get the exact length, width, and
depth before
selecting your size.

![nominal vs actual air filter size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-img-custom-filters-find-size.webp)

### ![Nominal Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-nominal-size.svg)  Nominal size

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x39x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x39x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x39x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x39x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x39x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x39x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x39x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x39x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x40.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x40.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x40.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x40.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x40.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x40.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x40.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x40.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x40x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x40x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x40x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x40x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x40x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x40x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x40x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x40x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## How to find your air filter size?

Check the label on your current filter or use a tape measure to get the exact length, width, and
depth before
selecting your size.

![nominal vs actual air filter size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-img-custom-filters-find-size.webp)

### ![Nominal Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-nominal-size.svg)  Nominal size

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x41x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x41x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x41x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x41x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x41x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x41x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x41x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x41x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x42.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x42.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x42.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x42.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x42.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x42.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x42.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x42.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## How to find your air filter size?

Check the label on your current filter or use a tape measure to get the exact length, width, and
depth before

![nominal vs actual air filter size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-img-custom-filters-find-size.webp)

### ![Nominal Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-nominal-size.svg)  Nominal size

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x42x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x42x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x42x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x42x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x42x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x42x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x42x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x42x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x43.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x43.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x43.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x43.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x43.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x43.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x43.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x43.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x43x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x43x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x43x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x43x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x43x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x43x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x43x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x43x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

font below the

the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x44.5x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x44.5x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x44.5x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x44.5x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x44.5x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x44.5x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x44.5x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x44.5x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## Who is the 11x44x1a MERV 13 best for?

[MERV 13 filters](https://filterking.com/air-filter/merv-13) are ideal for homes where air quality is a top priority. They're ideal for households
with allergies, asthma, and respiratory issues. Using a MERV 13 filter can also help improve indoor air
quality in households with immunocompromised family members and homes with pets that require extra
protection.


Our MERV 13 filters are suitable for urban homes near traffic and light commercial spaces, such as
offices or medical waiting rooms and even clinics in some instances. Shared living spaces and rental
units may benefit from MERV 13 filters, as the filter is designed to capture even more particles than
alternative ratings.

## How to find your air filter size?

Check the label on your current filter or use a tape measure to get the exact length, width, and
depth before
selecting your size.

![nominal vs actual air filter size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-img-custom-filters-find-size.webp)

### ![Nominal Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-nominal-size.svg)  Nominal size

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### How often should I replace my 11x44x1 air filter?

You should replace most 11x44x1 air filters every 30 to 90 days depending on your specific needs and circumstances. In households with asthma or allergies, replace your air filter every 6 weeks. If you have pets, replace it every 2 months. If you have young children, replace it every 2 to 3 months.


### What happens if I use the wrong size air filter?

Using the wrong size air filter can lead to poorer air quality and cause problems for your HVAC system. If the air filter size is too small, unfiltered air can bypass the filter and allow for dust to enter your HVAC system.


### Can I cut a larger filter to fit my 11x44x1 filter slot?

No, never cut air filters to fit your filter slot if you’ve ordered the wrong size. Cutting damages the filter frame and media, creates gaps for air bypass, and reduces filtration effectiveness. If you've ordered the wrong size, Filter King offers a 30-day money back guarantee, so you can easily return or exchange your filter for the correct size.


### Are expensive 11x44x1 air filters worth the extra cost?

In many cases it may be worth the extra cost, although it largely depends on your specific needs and circumstances. Higher-quality 11x44x1 filters often provide better filtration, last longer, and protect your HVAC system more effectively, meaning that the investment pays off through better air quality and reduced system maintenance costs.


### Can I run my HVAC system without a 11x44x1 filter temporarily?

No, never run your HVAC system without a filter, even temporarily. Running it without a filter allows dust, debris, and particles to enter your system, which can lead to expensive damage to components like the blower motor and evaporator coils.


### Will a MERV 13 11x44x1 filter restrict airflow too much?

A MERV 13 11x44x1 filter may restrict airflow in some of the older or lower-capacity HVAC systems, while most modern residential systems should handle a MERV filter without issues. If you notice reduced airflow, longer heating/cooling cycles, or increased energy bills after installing a MERV 13 filter, consider changing to a MERV 11 instead.

## How to find your air filter size?

Check the label on your current filter or use a tape measure to get the exact length, width, and
depth before
selecting your size.

![nominal vs actual air filter size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-img-custom-filters-find-size.webp)

### ![Nominal Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-nominal-size.svg)  Nominal size

**Nominal size** is what you normally see printed on the label. This is usually
a rounded
size which is often **not the true size** of your filter.


### ![Actual Size](https://filterking.com/img/product/p-icon-actual-size.svg)  Actual size

**Actual size is the true size** of the air filter, usually written in smaller
font below the
nominal size.


### Measuring

Measure your current air filter or the length, width, and depth of the opening slot to get
the actual size. Round it up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size.
